review.headline: A wild Pirc where both sides threw away material and the final blunders at 27.Ne4 and 28.Kg2 decided it

sections.text: You met the Pirc with a big centre, then went for a kingside space grab with 6.h3 and 7.g4. It didn't work: 8.Bg2?! allowed 8...Bxe4??, but 9.O-O?? missed 9.g5, and after 9...Bxd5 you were behind (-2.5 after 10.b3?).
11.Bb2? and 12.Qe2?! kept falling behind, and 11...hxg4 took the pawn structure apart. Credit to Black though: 12...e4?? gave back a lot (from -5.8 to -1.7), and you were back in the game.

Your best chess came at 17.fxe5!, which opened the f-file and uncovered the rook on f1, a discovered attack. After 18.Nxf7? you forked queen and rook, but 18...Qd3?? and 19.Qxd3! let you take the queen. Good punishing move.
Then it went wrong again. 20.Nxe5?? threw away a huge edge, 24.Rxf6! was good, but 27.Ne4?? missed 27.Rxd6+, and 28.Kg2?? left you at -5.8. 28.Rxd6+ was the move both times.

review.turning_point: At move 27 you had +4.0 available and Black had walked into 27...Re3+, but 27.Ne4?? missed 27.Rxd6+, and 28.Kg2?? finished it.
review.focus: At 27.Ne4 and 28.Kg2, you were responding to checks without checking captures. When you have a rook-for-bishop capture with check like 28.Rxd6+, calculate it first.

review.headline: You built a big advantage against the Hungarian, then let it leak away until 29...Bxc3

sections.text: As Black against 1.g3 you set up in the centre with 1...e5, 2...d5 and 3...Nf6. When White traded with 5.Bxf6?? you recaptured with 5...Qxf6!, the best reply, and from there you were comfortably better. Giving up the bishop pair with 7.Bh3 Bxh3 was fine for you, and you built a kingside pawn storm with 10...h5, 11...g5 and 12...h4.

The engine rated you around +4 by move 13, so this was a position to convert calmly. 13...h3?? let a lot of that go (+4.8 to +2.0); 13...d4 14.cxd4 hxg3 was the stronger break. You did get a nice moment later with 16...Nxe5!, picking the best reply to 16.Ne5?.
The next drift came at 21...f3??, which took the evaluation from +2.5 to level. White returned the favour with 22.e3?? and 24.Qb5+??, but 26...Qa3? and 27...Rd6? kept you from regaining control.
Then 29...Bxc3?? put you at -5.2. After 30.Qxc3 the queen hit both your queen on b2 and the rook on h8, a fork that cost material (-3). 29...Rhd8 was the calm alternative.

review.turning_point: 13...h3?? was the first big letdown at +4.8, but the game was decided at 29...Bxc3??, which allowed 30.Qxc3 to attack your queen and rook at once.
review.focus: At move 29, before taking 29...Bxc3, check which of your pieces the recapture would attack. Looking for opponent forks on every capture saves games like this.

review.headline: A Scandinavian where you punished one error, then missed the winning check at move 15

sections.text: This was a Scandinavian where Black's queen came out early after 2.exd5. After 3...Qe6+ you chose 4.Qe2?!, which allowed the queen trade and took your small edge down to +0.3. You then developed sensibly with 5.Ngxe2, 6.g3 and 7.Bg2, and the position stayed level.

10.d3?? was your first real slip and put you at -1.9, but 10...Nd4?? gave it straight back. You found the right reply with 11.Nxd4!, a clean way to punish the error, and the evaluation returned to about +0.9.

The game turned at move 14. After 14...Ne7?? you were at +4.9. The move was 15.Nxe7+, which uncovers the bishop on g2 against c6 as a discovered attack, and the engine line 15.Nxe7+ Bxe7 16.Bxc6 bxc6 17.Rxe7 shows you coming out ahead. Instead 15.c4?? allowed 15...Nxd5, and with material at -3 the advantage was gone.

After that you were defending. 18.Ba5? slipped further, and 21.Bh6?? left you facing 21...Rxe1+ with material down to -6. 21.Be3 was the safer move there. A fair fight in the opening and a won position in the middle that slipped away in one move.

review.turning_point: After 14...Ne7?? you stood at +4.9, but 15.c4?? missed 15.Nxe7+ with its discovered attack from g2, and after 15...Nxd5 the evaluation was -0.2.
review.focus: Before every quiet move, list your checks and captures first. At move 15 the check 15.Nxe7+ was the whole game.
